references.text: The spies explored the land for forty days, which is the basis for the punishment of forty years.
Ezekiel receives the same principle: one day for each year, as a symbolic act representing Israel's sin.
The psalm refers to the forty years in the wilderness and God's anger over the people's disobedience.
Moses speaks to the people in the fortieth year, confirming the fulfillment of the punishment's duration.
It describes that it took thirty-eight years from Kadesh-Barnea until the entire warrior generation had died out.
Joshua confirms that Israel wandered forty years in the wilderness until the entire warrior generation had died.
The Letter to the Hebrews refers to the wilderness generation that was not allowed to enter rest because of unbelief.
Stephen mentions the forty years in the wilderness in his speech about Israel's history.
Paul refers to God bearing with the people for forty years in the wilderness.
The context describing who would die in the wilderness and not enter the land.
